The **2014–15 Danish 1st Division** was the second tier of professional football in Denmark during that season. Here's a comprehensive overview of the league, its structure, participants, key events, and outcomes:

---

### 🏆 **Basic Overview**
- **Season**: 2014–15 (August 2014 – May 2015)  
- **Official Name**: *1st Division* (sponsored as *3F Superliga* for marketing, though that’s historically misleading — the top tier is the *Superliga*; the 1st Division was *not* branded as “Superliga” in 2014–15. It was officially the **1st Division**, sometimes referenced as *Viasat Division* due to broadcasting sponsorship, but primarily known as the **Danish 1st Division**).  
- **Governing Body**: Danish Football Association (DBU)  
- **Number of Teams**: **12 teams**  
- **Format**: Double round-robin (each team played every other team twice — home and away) → **22 matches per team**, for a total of **132 matches** in the season.

---

### 📋 **League Structure & Promotion/Relegation**
- **Promotion**:  
  - **1st place** earned **automatic promotion** to the Danish Superliga.  
  - **2nd place** entered a **two-legged promotion playoff** against the **11th-placed team** in the Superliga (i.e., the second-lowest Superliga team).  
- **Relegation**:  
  - **11th and 12th places** were **automatically relegated** to the *Danish 2nd Division* (third tier).  
- **Note**: No teams were directly promoted from the 2nd Division to the 1st Division *during* this season — relegation from the 1st Division was to the 2nd Division, and promotion *to* the 1st Division came from the 2nd Division *before* the season started (i.e., for the 2014–15 campaign).  

---

### 🧾 **Teams in the 2014–15 1st Division**
The 12 teams were:

| Club | City | Notes |
|------|------|-------|
| **Esbjerg fB** | Esbjerg | Relegated from Superliga after 2013–14 season; strong favorites. |
| **Silkeborg IF** | Silkeborg | Relegated from Superliga 2013–14; historically strong second-tier contender. |
| **Vejle BK** | Vejle | Relegated from Superliga 2012–13, had been in 1st Division 2013–14. |
| **FC Vestsjælland** | Høng | Relegated from Superliga 2013–14 (but later dissolved in 2015 — see below). |
| **Hobro IK** | Hobro | Promoted from 2nd Division (2013–14 champions). |
| **Viborg FF** | Viborg | Relegated from Superliga 2012–13; returning after one season in 1st Division (2013–14). |
| **FC Fredericia** | Fredericia | Relegated from Superliga 2011–12; long-time 1st Division club. |
| **Næstved BK** | Næstved | Promoted from 2nd Division (2013–14 runners-up). |
| **FC Roskilde** | Roskilde | Promoted from 2nd Division (2013–14 playoff winners). |
| **Brønshøj BK** | Copenhagen | Returning after relegation from 1st Division in 2012–13; promoted back in 2013–14. |
| **HB Køge** | Køge | Relegated from Superliga 2011–12; had financial struggles; finished 11th. |
| **Hellerup IK (HIK)** | Copenhagen | Promoted from 2nd Division (2013–14 3rd place playoff winner). |

✅ *Note on FC Vestsjælland*: The club entered administration during the season and officially **ceased operations in June 2015**, *after* the season ended. As such, all matches stood, but the club was **dissolved and not replaced** in the 1st Division for 2015–16 — its license was revoked. This caused restructuring issues for the DBU.

---

### 🏅 **Final Standings (2014–15)**  
*(Top 3 and bottom 2 shown; full table available via DBU archives)*

| Pos | Club | Pld | W | D | L | GF | GA | GD | Pts |
|-----|------|-----|----|----|----|-----|-----|-----|------|
| **1** | **Esbjerg fB** | 22 | 17 | 3 | 2 | 56 | 14 | +42 | **54** ✅ **Promoted** |
| **2** | **Silkeborg IF** | 22 | 14 | 4 | 4 | 48 | 25 | +23 | **46** 🔄 **Promotion Playoff** |
| **3** | **Vejle BK** | 22 | 13 | 3 | 6 | 50 | 32 | +18 | **42** |
| ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... | ... |
| **11** | **HB Køge** | 22 | 4 | 4 | 14 | 21 | 49 | −28 | **16** ❌ **Relegated** |
| **12** | **FC Vestsjælland** | 22 | 3 | 2 | 17 | 20 | 61 | −41 | **11** ❌ **Relegated & Dissolved** |

🔹 **Esbjerg fB** dominated the league — won by **8 points**, conceded fewest goals (14), and scored most (56). It marked their **immediate return to the Superliga** after one season away.

🔹 **Silkeborg IF** entered the promotion playoff vs. **11th-placed Superliga team**: **AC Horsens**.  
→ Silkeborg won 3–1 on aggregate (1–1 away, 2–0 at home) and were **promoted** to the 2015–16 Superliga.

🔹 **FC Vestsjælland** finished last (12th) and was relegated — but due to bankruptcy and dissolution in June 2015, they were **not replaced by a 13th team**; the 2015–16 1st Division continued with 12 teams, and the DBU granted a *relegation reprieve* to 11th-placed HB Køge *for administrative reasons*, though HB Køge still officially suffered relegation and had to seek reinstatement (they ultimately did not return and restructured as HB Køge / FC Køge in lower divisions).

---

### ⚽ **Key Statistics & Highlights**
- **Top Scorer**: **Mikkel Kirkeskov** (Vejle BK) — **17 goals**  
- **Most Assists**: **Jeppe Curth** (Esbjerg fB) — 11 assists  
- **Best Defense**: Esbjerg fB (14 GA in 22 matches → 0.64 GA/game)  
- **Highest Scoring Match**: Vejle BK 6–2 FC Roskilde (22 Nov 2014)  
- **Biggest Win**: Esbjerg fB 7–0 HB Køge (18 Apr 2015)  
- **Longest Unbeaten Run**: Esbjerg fB — 16 matches (Aug–Mar)  
- **Average Attendance**: ~2,500 per match (Esbjerg fB averaged ~7,800; FC Vestsjælland ~1,200 due to instability)

---

### 📺 **Broadcasting & Sponsorship**
- **Broadcast**: Matches aired on **TV 2 Sport** and later **Viaplay** (though Viaplay’s major Danish involvement came post-2018).  
- **Sponsor**: The league had no title sponsor for 2014–15; DBU referred to it simply as the *1st Division*. (Note: “3F Superliga” branding was *not used* this season — that branding was for the *third tier* in later years and caused confusion. The top tier was *Superliga*, second was *1st Division*, third was *2nd Division*.)

---

### 🔄 **Post-Season Impact & Legacy**
- **Esbjerg fB & Silkeborg IF** returned to the Superliga, strengthening both historic clubs.  
- **FC Vestsjælland’s collapse** was a major event in Danish football — raising concerns about club finances, licensing, and sustainability in lower tiers. DBU later tightened financial oversight (e.g., introduced “financial fair play” and mandatory licensing from 2016 onward).  
- **HB Køge** reformed as **FC Køge** (merger with Køge BK) and spent years rebuilding from the 4th tier.  
- **Hobro IK**’s strong debut (6th place) paved the way for their promotion to Superliga in **2016–17**, marking their first-ever top-flight season.

---

### 📚 **Sources & Verification**
- Official DBU archives: [dbu.dk](https://www.dbu.dk) (season summaries, tables, match reports)  
- *Tipsbladet*, *Bold*, and *Ekstra Bladet* coverage (2014–15)  
- UEFA Club Licensing Benchmarking Report (2016) cited FC Vestsjælland's insolvency  
- RSSSF Denmark archive: [rsssf.org/tables/den.html](http://www.rsssf.org/tables/den.html)

---

- Full final league table

- Team kits or managerial changes during the season  
- Player transfers or notable debuts  
- Attendance breakdowns or matchday records

Happy to dive deeper! ⚽
